source.title: Asymptotic Study of in-Context Learning with Random Transformers Through Equivalent Models

record.tranche_reason: Extends double-descent analysis to in-context learning error for a random Transformer with a nonlinear MLP head, rather than reproducing the original supervised-learning settings.
record.gate_note: Reports its own sample-size, hidden-dimension, and regularization sweeps of ICL error. The authors also compare the Transformer with a linear-attention baseline and an equivalent polynomial model. No epoch sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own sweeps of ICL error over hidden width m, training-sample count n and ridge λ in a random-feature Transformer (frozen first MLP layer, trained readout). It reports a fall-rise-fall curve peaking at m/n ≈ 1 and attenuation of the peak under regularization, so it tests double descent in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also conclude that the nonlinear MLP helps ICL only with a suitable activation, a sufficiently long context (ℓ ≳ d), and a suitable width or regularization.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic nonlinear-regression ICL tasks and a random Transformer with linear attention and a fixed random first MLP layer whose second layer is trained. It measures ICL error across hidden dimension, sample count, and regularization rather than reproducing the original supervised-learning experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported benefits of nonlinear MLPs depend on activation choice and target-function alignment; context length affects ICL error; regularization strength attenuates the width-sweep peak.
record.peer_reviewed: International Workshop on Machine Learning for Signal Processing
record.problems: The study concerns a simplified random Transformer and synthetic regression tasks. The reported curves are not accompanied in the text by numerical point values; uncertainty beyond a mean over 20 Monte Carlo runs is not stated. The sample-size curve is described as non-monotonic without locating the rise relative to interpolation.

untested.parts: Fully trained deep networks are not scaled; only random-feature readout width is varied.
There is no epoch or training-time sweep.
The exact location of the sample-wise rise relative to the interpolation threshold is not stated.
No effective-complexity measure is used across axes.
Label noise or variance as the driver is not tested (noise ρ is fixed at 0.01). Multiple peaks are not tested. Elimination under optimally tuned λ is not tested.
The study does not re-count effective parameters.

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is figure-based and given in the text only qualitatively, as means of 20 Monte Carlo runs. The setting is essentially random-features ridge regression on ICL features, so it extends the classical Belkin/Mei-Montanari random-features double descent rather than deep-network double descent.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests hidden dimension in a random Transformer ICL setting; it does not test deep-network model scaling in the original supervised-learning setting.
Training epochs or training time are not swept.
The sample-size sweep is reported as non-monotonic, but the text does not locate the increase relative to an interpolation threshold.
Only a random Transformer with a nonlinear MLP is tested; the claim across model classes is not broadly assessed.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, and sample count.
The regularization sweep tests attenuation of the peak, but does not test label-noise or variance as its driver, multiple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The study does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that makes the curve an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: random Transformer with a nonlinear MLP
rows.size_stated: hidden dimension m; interpolation threshold reported at m/n ≈ 1
rows.stage_stated: first MLP layer randomly initialized and fixed; second layer trained
rows.operation_detail: Sweep hidden dimension m and measure ICL error.
rows.value: Error decreases in the under-parameterized regime, peaks near m/n ≈ 1, then declines in the over-parameterized regime.
rows.uncertainty: Mean of 20 Monte Carlo runs; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.note: The authors describe this as double descent with respect to model size. The reported size axis is hidden dimension m.
rows.check: The model is a random-features regression: the first layer is frozen and only the linear readout is trained. This matches the Belkin-style model-class claim (V4), not deep-network model-wise scaling of fully trained networks (V1), so the V1 link is removed.

rows.subject: Transformer with a nonlinear MLP
rows.stage_stated: first MLP layer randomly initialized and fixed; second layer trained
rows.operation_detail: Sweep the number of training samples n and measure ICL error.

conditions.value: Figure 1a: ReLU target; Figure 1b: tanh target; two MLP activation functions are shown

rows.value: The authors report a non-monotonic trend in ICL error as the number of training samples varies.
rows.uncertainty: Mean of 20 Monte Carlo runs; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.note: The text does not specify where the error rises relative to an interpolation threshold or give numerical values for the rise.
rows.check: The text says only that error is non-monotonic in n and that this is due to small λ. The location of the rise is not stated, though interpolation would sit at n = m = d². The authors' attribution to weak regularization also bears on V6.

rows.subject: Transformer with a nonlinear MLP
rows.stage_stated: first MLP layer randomly initialized and fixed; second layer trained
rows.operation_detail: Vary regularization strength λ and measure ICL error against hidden dimension.

conditions.value: λ varied; specific values not stated in the text

rows.baseline: The low-regularization curve has a sharp peak near the interpolation threshold.
rows.value: As λ increases, the curve becomes more stable and the peak is attenuated.
rows.uncertainty: Mean of 20 Monte Carlo runs; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.note: The text reports attenuation, not elimination of the peak or an optimally tuned regularization setting.
rows.check: The peak is attenuated and smoothed as λ grows; elimination at an optimal λ is not reported. The λ values are not given in the text.

relationships.condition: Random-feature Transformer readout on synthetic nonlinear ICL regression, λ = 1e-8, ReLU and tanh activations
relationships.reason: ICL error falls, peaks near m/n ≈ 1, then falls again as width grows (r1).
relationships.display_finding: ICL error initially fell, peaked near m/n = 1, and fell again as width increased.

relationships.condition: Sample-count sweep with m = d² and small λ = 1e-8
relationships.reason: The authors report non-monotonic ICL error in n, so more samples raise error somewhere. This rests on text only, with the location relative to n = m unstated (r2).
relationships.display_finding: In-context learning error varied nonmonotonically with n, including increases with more samples, without a specified peak location relative to n = m.

relationships.condition: Width sweep with ReLU activation and increasing λ; sample sweep at small λ
relationships.reason: Larger λ attenuates and smooths the peak, and the authors attribute the sample-wise non-monotonicity to small λ (r3, r2). Full elimination is not shown.
relationships.display_finding: Larger λ attenuated and smoothed the peak, while sample-wise nonmonotonicity was attributed to small λ; complete elimination was unestablished.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
